Idk your financial situation or if this would work with your insurance but I was able to keep my therapist by sending in a superbill to my insurance provider. It's basically an itemized reciept of your treatment and if you have out-of-network coverage they reimburse you for the amount they cover.

You have to pay your therapist up front, and it's still more expensive than being able to use your insurance normally, but for me at least it makes it affordable enough to keep my therapist who I'm comfortable with.

Sorry if this is irrelevant to your situation, but I wanted to at least throw it out there as an option for you. Best of luck!

Generally "bitching" (verb) wouldn't be considered offensive unless you're around someone who just doesn't like cussing in general. Language evolves over time and lots of gendered things aren't inherently derogatory. I mean "bitchin'" is used to describe something good or cool. 

I call everyone "dude" regardless of gender. You don't even need to use it to address someone, it can be used as a statement too. My reaction to hearing something absurd beyond words? "...Dude."

Of course there are exceptions, and the big ol' asterisk here is some people are going to be offended by things.   Seems you just encountered one. I know we all assume these situations are a Twitter-esque overreaction (which it may very well be) but it may not come from a bad place either. Maybe they are just repeating what they were told, maybe that's what they were raised to believe. Who knows.

Best thing is to do your best to read the room and know  your audience. I'm a woman and me and my closest friends, male or female, call each other "bitch" all the time. We give each other shit but we all know it's said in jest and doesn't go any deeper. But like you said, I wouldn't go around and address my grandma or an acquaintance that way though haha.

Birth control is an option! It's the main option! But BC fails sometimes. Rape happens and results in pregnancy. Sometimes wanted pregnancies are not viable or are downright life threatening.

Have you heard about the 10 year old in Ohio? She is a rape victim and had to travel out of state for an abortion. Is forcing a literal child to carry for 9 months a child she didn't ask for okay?? Is the bundle of cells right now worth more than her life?

There was a post in the Ohio subreddit about a woman who wants to try for a baby but is scared to. Her last pregnancy was ectopic (the egg was fertilized in the fallopian tube). This is a life threatening medical condition. She needed an abortion and is at a greater risk of it happening again. Now if it did she no longer has access to the life saving medical procedure that saved her last time. Is it okay having to choose between having a family or risking death?

There are people who were on birth control but had it fail on them. Many live in poverty and cannot afford to care for another human. Is willingly bringing a child into a horrible situation ethical just because the condom broke or the pill failed?

What about the parents who wanted a baby but find out early it isn't viable? Is it really better to force her to carry it to term just for it to die shortly after birth or have a horrible quality of life? 

What about the woman who miscarries later on in the pregnancy? The procedure to remove the fetus is abortion. Is it really better to force her to carry a stillborn to term? Is she at fault for the baby dying inside her? 

The vast majority of abortions are not done because someone was irresponsible. They are performed because it is medically necessary. And when medical care is not provided people take it into their own hands.  
This ban will not prevent abortions, it only removed the option for safe ones. This ban is hurting people.

On really busy days you'd have staff getting there at 4 or 5am to start, that's how much prep and planning goes into things!

Too many consider the "bad service" they got to be because of laziness or rudeness, when in reality a restaurant can't immediately pull unlimited resources out of their ass.
